name: Recovery labels
status: Prepared for independent review; no novelty or empirical certification
novelty_confidence: Uncertain; generic automata and milestone mechanisms are established
hypothesis: History-conditioned sets of efficient acceptable recovery actions reduce teacher error and improve held-out recovery compared with matched geometric, nDTW, reversible-chunk and reward-machine controls.
gap: Geometric rejoining can alias histories with different unfinished instruction obligations; empirical incidence is unknown.
additional_supplied_locators: HAMT extended PDF p 9 Table 7; p 16 Sections B.1-B.2, existing R2R-Back task/protocol
mechanism: Annotate event witnesses and remaining state, construct training-only graph-times-instruction-state oracle, supervise a set of tied efficient actions, and optionally condition the navigator on a learned soft instruction-state token.

formal_variables.b_phi: categorical state estimator from observed history

objective: -log(sum_a_in_Y pi(a|history,instruction,b)) + lambda*(-log b(q_true)) plus matched ordinary-task loss; unresolved labels masked or separately partial-labelled.
novelty_argument: Potentially a validated off-path teacher/annotation protocol and controlled intervention in photorealistic VLN, not a new automaton, progress monitor, backtracking mechanism or imitation-learning principle.
expected_benefits: Better ordered-obligation completion if the affected slice is common and observable
minimal_changes: Optional state-token head after label-only experiment
datasets: R2R-Back with its existing stage-aware success/full-route SPL
baselines: common-action-interface DUET SPL and nDTW teachers
controls: Same sampled states and action candidates
Same human labels and optimizer updates
FGR2R/M-TRACK reconstructed mechanisms labelled paper-derived; released navigation paths are incomplete
cheapest_test: Independently annotate remaining obligations and acceptable actions at natural deviations and same-pose/different-history pairs; compare existing teacher error before training.
assumptions: A bounded instruction grammar has reliable event semantics
Training-only graph and event supervision are available
anticipated_confounders: Synthetic-pair prevalence mistaken for natural frequency
empirical_status: No benchmark. One original finite product-graph example executed.
prerequisites: Validate paper-derived milestone/chunk baselines; do not assume incomplete releases are runnable
review_questions: Is the teacher intervention meaningfully different from existing reward-machine or partial-label imitation methods?
Does the action-set loss admit harmful degenerate solutions?
Can all controls share the same feasible action set?
logical_status: Formulation proposed; independently audited status pending assignment 08
implementation_status: No proposed system implemented; pinned starting source inspected within recorded scope

name: Validity and difficulty
status: Prepared for independent review; no novelty or empirical certification
novelty_confidence: Uncertain; likely an empirical/data contribution unless witness supervision adds distinct value
hypothesis: At fixed generated pool, accepted count and training compute, independent semantic-validity selection that preserves valid difficult pairs improves held-out semantic following beyond success/compatibility/noisy-label selection.
gap: Navigator success and pair validity are different variables; current selection can in principle reject valid hard pairs or retain invalid easy pairs, with prevalence unmeasured.
additional_supplied_locators: GSA-VLN Appendix A.2, PDF pp 16-17: speaker splits, environment-specific DUET selection and visual instruction correction
Meta-Explore supplementary p 4, Table 2 and Section C.3: category processing changes results
mechanism: Use blinded human audit and clause-to-view/transition witnesses to train a validity scorer separate from a frozen policy difficulty measure; select equal-count difficulty strata and train the unchanged navigator.

formal_variables.D_k: disjoint exhaustive eligible-pool partition with declared semantic/difficulty assignment

objective: Validity scorer: three-way pair CE, clause-status CE, and masked -log(sum of attention on adjudicated witness units). Selection maximizes sum_i s_i*p(valid_i) under fixed B and strata; ordinary action CE trains the unchanged navigator. These ordinary losses/optimization are not claimed novel or guaranteed.
novelty_argument: Potentially a measured validity-versus-competence separation and witness-supervised selector under fixed budgets; generic filtering, curriculum and reweighting are prior art.
minimal_changes: Frozen difficulty logging; unchanged navigator loss
datasets: One frozen generated R2R/RxR training pool
baselines: GSA model selection plus visual correction, with correction/pool changes separated
controls: Same accepted count and token/update budget
Same path/scene mix or explicit factorial controls
Same human audit labels for learned controls
Count additional clause/witness annotation effort; equal pair count does not ensure equal human effort
cheapest_test: Blinded validity-by-difficulty audit; compare false acceptance/rejection at equal acceptance rate before large-scale training.
falsification: Validity adds no discrimination beyond existing selectors
Hard subset is mainly noisy labels
Downstream gains vanish under equal budgets
assumptions: Semantic validity can be adjudicated for enough examples
Audit labels are independent of navigator scores
anticipated_confounders: Selection thresholds tuned on final test
Benchmark construction conditioned on a navigator or same-scene selector; distinct from downstream navigator leakage
empirical_status: Untested; no audit labels, model training or navigation execution.
prerequisites: Frozen navigator checkpoint or difficulty logs
review_questions: Is there contribution beyond established data-quality/curriculum methods?
Does witness supervision improve validity at the same human-label budget?
Can original success filters be faithfully implemented without missing source?
logical_status: Formulation proposed; independently audited status pending assignment 08
implementation_status: No proposed system implemented; pinned starting source inspected within recorded scope

name: Joint future events
status: Speculative candidate prepared for independent review; may be rejected
novelty_confidence: Low pending independent search; future QA and decision-aware compression already exist
hypothesis: For observable decisions requiring two ordered events on one continuation, joint-event prediction improves candidate ranking over equally sized additive future semantics with matched data and labels.
gap: Additive expected future features can preserve timewise marginals while losing ordered co-occurrence; actual NavQ target collisions and policy impact are unknown.
mechanism: Predict K event occurrence probabilities and KxK ordered pair probabilities under one specified continuation policy/horizon; use a matched navigator readout and test held-out compositions.

formal_variables.Z_i^k: grounded event k at future step i
formal_variables.J_kl: probability of event k then event l on one continuation

objective: Masked BCE for single and joint event targets from identical continuation samples; compare additive features, sequences, future QA and direct value at equal budget. Raw heads are not a coherent trajectory distribution; audit J<=min(p) violations and compare bounded/projection variants.
novelty_argument: Possible branch-consistent temporal-event target and controlled VLN study; not generic semantic prediction, world-model sufficiency, distributional prediction or low-rank compression.
expected_benefits: Retain a specific non-additive future distinction
Reuse compact event evidence across paired order queries
minimal_changes: Fixed-candidate scoring harness before closed-loop integration
datasets: Labelled branch continuations from training scenes
Ordered route extension on R2R/RxR; original NavQ tasks are object-goal
controls: Same continuation samples and event labels
Fixed continuation policy for first ranking test
cheapest_test: Oracle-representation readout on independently labelled correlated branches; stop if joint statistics provide no headroom, then test whether observable history predicts the distinction.
falsification: Future-QA or sequence baseline matches at cost
Benefit is only capacity or labels
assumptions: Events and order can be reliably grounded
The needed distinction is observable or statistically predictable
Continuation policy is declared and sufficiently supported
anticipated_confounders: Task shift from object-goal to route following
Confusing expected event probability with reachability/guarantee
empirical_status: One original finite arithmetic counterexample executed; no NavQ/model/benchmark execution.
review_questions: Is this equivalent to predictive-state/successor or semantic-QA prior art?
Do the probabilities refer to a consistent continuation policy?
Can the target be learned without extra hidden information?

implementation_status: No proposed system implemented; pinned starting source inspected within recorded scope

name: Failure-aware memory
status: Prepared for independent review; no novelty or empirical certification
novelty_confidence: Uncertain; typed/provenance/negative memory and Bayesian negative evidence are established
hypothesis: Separating identity error from control/arrival failure before persistent negative writes reduces harmful suppression and improves repeated navigation beyond no-write/quarantine/tri-state controls at fixed memory and feedback.
gap: Terminal failure does not uniquely locate the failed semantic claim; an inspected outcome-to-false-positive write path may misattribute failures, but prevalence is unmeasured. Native PSG ObjectNav category claims and any added specific-instance task must remain distinct.
mechanism: Train separate masked identity/approach/completion attribution heads with controlled paired evidence; write negative semantics only with identity-specific contradiction evidence, otherwise quarantine or update a route/control claim.
objective: Sum of masked BCE attribution losses, optionally identity invariance on verified controller-only paired interventions; semantic negative gate qD>=tauD and W=1. No independence or exclusivity assumption across causes.
novelty_argument: Potentially failure-attribution training/evaluation for persistent memory; fixing one wrong write rule or adding source/uncertain tags alone is not a scientific mechanism.
expected_benefits: Reduce later rejection of correct targets

files: RAG manager write/read interface: inspect exact implementation before edits

minimal_changes: Shadow logging of writes before changing actions
Attribution wrapper and explicit quarantine path
datasets: Repeated tasks with randomized scene episode orders
controls: Scene-disjoint calibration and held-out order tests
cheapest_test: Replay valid-category/control-failure versus incorrect-category/control-success traces; measure false semantic writes and later suppression. Same-class different-instance errors belong only to a separately specified instance-goal extension.
falsification: Cause labels need unavailable privileged evidence
assumptions: Failure causes have observable evidence in sufficient cases
Deployable witness is linked observed evidence plus predicted contradiction, not ground-truth truth certification
anticipated_confounders: Release bug fix mistaken for research novelty
Conflating native category ObjectNav with specific-instance goals
empirical_status: Original truth-table counterexample executed; no trace audit, attribution training or repeated navigation benchmark.
review_questions: Does simple quarantine already remove the harm?
Can identity-error evidence be inferred without privileged inputs?
Is attribution different from existing fault diagnosis/belief update methods?
